analysis.title: Mirion Technologies Inc. (MIR): Orders robust, medium-term margins in focus
key_insights: MIR reported 3Q26 adj. EBITDA of $64.8mn, below GS's $68.1mn estimate, driven by weaker Nuclear & Safety margins (25.7% vs GS 27.8%), partly offset by Medical (37.8% vs GS 36.7%).
Management said Nuclear & Safety margin would have been 28.3% excluding Paragon and the prior-year incentive compensation adjustment, a modest y/y expansion.
Organic orders rose 62% y/y, led by +105% in Nuclear Power. TTM organic orders are +37%, with the installed base the largest contributor to dollar growth.
Total backlog is $1.25bn vs $816mn a year ago. $292mn is expected to convert in 4Q26 and $443mn in 2027, about $735mn combined, more than $200mn higher than at the same point last year.

MIR lowered its 2026 adj. EBITDA guide to $285-$292mn (from $285-$300mn) and narrowed adj. EPS guidance to $0.50-$0.54 (from $0.48-$0.55), based on organic growth of +7-8%. Adjusted FCF guidance rose to $170-$185mn (prior $155-$175mn).
The guide implies Q4 Nuclear & Safety organic growth of high-teens or better, which GS considers reasonable given backlog coverage and Paragon's December results entering organic growth.
The Medical guide assumes mid-single-digit-plus growth, supported by software revenue momentum and an easy comp (-5% organic in 4Q25).

Management withdrew its 2028 margin target of 30%, citing softer Medical organic growth versus the original assumptions, a longer path to margin accretion for parts of Paragon, and greater AI/cybersecurity investment.
Management pointed to 100-200bps of annual margin expansion as the new focus and plans a more mature long-term framework at next year's investor day.

GS lowered FY26/FY27/FY28 EBITDA estimates to $288mn/$330mn/$375mn (from $290mn/$335mn/$377mn), kept the Buy rating and the $20 12-month PT, and cut the Q5-Q8 EBITDA multiple to 17.0x from 18.0x. The PT implies a FY28 FCF yield of about 4.5%.

market_movers.rationale: Orders and backlog remain strong, but the withdrawn 2028 margin target and lower EBITDA estimates shift the debate to margins. The PT is unchanged after rolling forward a quarter and cutting the multiple to 17.0x from 18.0x.

tension_points.bull_case: Orders are up 62% y/y, backlog is $1.25bn, and Nuclear & Safety margin would have been 28.3% excluding Paragon and the prior-year incentive compensation adjustment. Management sees 100-200bps of annual margin expansion.
tension_points.bear_case: Management withdrew the 2028 30% margin target, citing softer Medical growth, a longer path to margin accretion for parts of Paragon, and higher AI/cybersecurity investment. The 2026 EBITDA guide was cut at the top end.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Weaker organic growth, lower operating leverage or dilutive M&A, the risks GS names.

theme_stances.key_argument: Orders and backlog conversion remain strong, but the focus shifts to margins after the 2028 target was withdrawn.
